Chrome/Edge desktop: ~60% of free disk (multi-GB typical)\n173\t * - Firefox: ~10% of disk, capped ~10 GB\n174\t * - Safari/iOS: ~1 GB before prompting\n175\t *\n176\t * **IMPORTANT:** These estimates are ADVISORY, not guarantees. Safari's\n177\t * estimate is particularly unreliable. Always handle quota exhaustion mid-transfer\n178\t * even if pre-flight checks pass.\n179\t *\n180\t * @returns Storage quota estimate or null if not supported\n181\t */\n182\texport async function estimateStorageQuota(): Promise<StorageQuotaEstimate | null> {\n183\t  try {\n184\t    if (!navigator.storage || !navigator.storage.estimate) {\n185\t      console.warn('[Storage] navigator.storage.estimate() not supported');\n186\t      return null;\n187\t    }\n188\t\n189\t    const estimate = await navigator.storage.estimate();\n190\t\n191\t    if (!estimate || estimate.quota == null || estimate.usage == null) {\n192\t      console.warn('[Storage] Invalid storage estimate:', estimate);\n193\t      return null;\n194\t    }\n195\t\n196\t    const quota = estimate.quota;\n197\t    const usage = estimate.usage;\n198\t    const available = quota - usage;\n199\t\n200\t    return {\n201\t      quota,\n202\t      usage,\n203\t      available,\n204\t    };\n205\t  } catch (error) {\n206\t    console.error('[Storage] Failed to estimate storage quota:', error);\n207\t    return null;\n208\t  }\n209\t}\n210\t\n211\t/**\n212\t * Calculate compression staging buffer for file transfer (bf-4d6).\n213\t *\n214\t * During compression and encoding, the sender needs temporary working space.\n215\t * This accounts for:\n216\t * - Compressed data staging\n217\t * - Block encoding buffers\n218\t * - Fountain code matrix storage (I6a: 1 MB working set)\n219\t * - Temporary artifacts during transfer\n220\t *\n221\t * **Formula:** staging = fileSize * 0.15 + 10 MB\n222\t * - 15% overhead for compression staging (conservative estimate)\n223\t * - 10 MB fixed buffer for codec working sets\n224\t *\n225\t * @param fileSize - Size of the file to transfer in bytes\n226\t * @returns Required staging buffer in bytes\n227\t */\n228\texport function calculateCompressionStagingBuffer(fileSize: number): number {\n229\t  const COMPRESSION_OVERHEAD = 0.15; // 15% overhead for compression staging\n230\t  const CODEC_BUFFER = 10 * 1024 * 1024; // 10 MB fixed codec buffer\n231\t\n232\t  return Math.ceil(fileSize * COMPRESSION_OVERHEAD) + CODEC_BUFFER;\n233\t}\n234\t\n235\t/**\n236\t * Check if there's enough storage capacity for a file transfer (bf-4d6 F1).\n237\t *\n238\t * **Pre-flight validation:** Call this BEFORE accepting a file to avoid\n239\t * discovering quota exhaustion hours into a transfer.\n240\t *\n241\t * **Safety margin:** Multiplies required space by 1.5 to account for:\n242\t * - OPFS filesystem overhead\n243\t * - Metadata storage\n244\t * - Quota estimate inaccuracies (especially Safari)\n245\t * - Platform-specific quota variations\n246\t *\n247\t * @param fileSize - Size of the file to transfer in bytes\n248\t * @param additionalSpace - Optional additional space to reserve in bytes\n249\t * @returns Storage capacity check result\n250\t */\n251\texport async function checkStorageCapacity(\n252\t  fileSize: number,\n253\t  additionalSpace: number = 0\n254\t): Promise<StorageCapacityResult> {\n255\t  // Default to assuming capacity if estimate unavailable (don't block on unsupported platforms)\n256\t  const estimate = await estimateStorageQuota();\n257\t\n258\t  if (!estimate) {\n259\t    console.warn('[Storage] Unable to estimate quota, proceeding with caution');\n260\t    return {\n261\t      hasCapacity: true, // Optimistic default - let the transfer attempt\n262\t      estimate: {\n263\t        quota: 0,\n264\t        usage: 0,\n265\t        available: 0,\n266\t      },\n267\t      requiredSpace: fileSize + additionalSpace,\n268\t      availableSpace: 0,\n269\t    };\n270\t  }\n271\t\n272\t  // Calculate required space with staging buffer and safety margin\n273\t  const stagingBuffer = calculateCompressionStagingBuffer(fileSize);\n274\t  const baseRequired = fileSize + stagingBuffer + additionalSpace;\n275\t  const SAFETY_MARGIN = 1.5; // 50% safety margin for quota estimate inaccuracies\n276\t  const requiredSpace = Math.ceil(baseRequired * SAFETY_MARGIN);\n277\t\n278\t  const hasCapacity = estimate.available >= requiredSpace;\n279\t\n280\t  if (!hasCapacity) {\n281\t    const shortfall = requiredSpace - estimate.available;\n282\t    const error = `Insufficient storage capacity. Required: ${formatBytes(requiredSpace)}, Available: ${formatBytes(estimate.available)}, Shortfall: ${formatBytes(shortfall)}`;\n283\t\n284\t    console.warn('[Storage] Capacity check failed:', error);\n285\t\n286\t    return {\n287\t      hasCapacity: false,\n288\t      estimate,\n289\t      requiredSpace,\n290\t      availableSpace: estimate.available,\n291\t      error,\n292\t    };\n293\t  }\n294\t\n295\t  console.log('[Storage] Capacity check passed:', {\n296\t    required: formatBytes(requiredSpace),\n297\t    available: formatBytes(estimate.available),\n298\t    margin: formatBytes(estimate.available - requiredSpace),\n299\t  });\n300\t\n301\t  return {\n302\t    hasCapacity: true,\n303\t    estimate,\n304\t    requiredSpace,\n305\t    availableSpace: estimate.available,\n306\t  };\n307\t}\n308\t\n309\t/**\n310\t * Format bytes as human-readable string (e.g., \"1.5 GB\").\n311\t */\n312\tfunction formatBytes(bytes: number): string {\n313\t  const units = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB'];\n314\t  let size = bytes;\n315\t  let unitIndex = 0;\n316\t\n317\t  while (size >= 1024 && unitIndex < units.length - 1) {\n318\t    size /= 1024;\n319\t    unitIndex++;\n320\t  }\n321\t\n322\t  return `${size.toFixed(unitIndex === 0 ? 0 : 1)} ${units[unitIndex]}`;\n323\t}\n324\t\n325\t/**\n326\t * OPFS-based storage manager implementation.\n327\t console.log('[Storage:Deletion] Starting deletion', {\n467\t      streamId,\n468\t      filename: filename || '(unknown)',\n469\t      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\n470\t    });\n471\t\n472\t    try {\n473\t      const outputDir = await this.getOutputDirectory();\n474\t      const filePath = this.getFilePath(streamId);\n475\t      const metadataPath = }\n591\t              if (isOld) {\n592\t                reasons.push(`exceeds maximum age (${Math.round(age / 1000 / 60)} minutes > ${Math.round(this.config.maxOrphanAge / 1000 / 60)}             isInactive,\n600\t                isOld,\n601\t              });\n602\t            }\n603\t          } catch (e) {\n604\t            // Handle corrupted metadata gracefully\n605\t The core issue: **CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee across browser restarts, updates, or platforms**, making the sender non-stateless when compression is enabled.\n\n**Decision:** Resume is explicitly **unsupported when compression is enabled**. The beacon carries a `RESUME_DISABLED` flag to signal this to receivers.\n\n## The Failure Chain\n\n### Step 1: Initial Compression\n```\nFile → CompressionStream → Staging (OPFS) → Blocks → Hashes → Frames\n```\n- D8 compresses the file to a staging area in OPFS\n- The compressed bytes are cut into fixed-size blocks\n- Each block is hashed to create the manifest\n- These hashes become the source of truth for the receiver\n\n### Step 2: Transfer Interrupted\n- Sender crashes, user stops transfer, or browser backgrounding occurs\n- Receiver persists bitmap of completed blocks (D22)\n- Both sides resume capability depends on identical block hashes\n\n### Step 3: Privacy Reaping (E11, T4a)\n- On sender restart, E11 reaps abandoned staging files\n- T4a privacy requirement mandates wiping staging on completion/cancel\n- **The compressed staging file is deleted**\n\n### Step 4: Sender Restart Attempts Resume\n```\nSender restarts → staging gone → must re-compress\n```\n- Sender attempts to resume the same session\n- Needs the same `streamId` and the same block hashes\n- **Problem:** Must re-compress because staging was reaped\n\n### Step 5: Re-compression Produces Different Bytes\n```\nSame file + CompressionStream → different compressed bytes (potentially)\n```\n**Why this can happen:**\n1. **Browser updates** → Different compression algorithm version\n2. **Different platforms** → Chrome vs Firefox vs Safari implementations\n3. **Compression parameters** → Different level, strategy, or metadata\n4. **Timestamp metadata** → Gzip includes modification time if file handle varies\n\n### Step 6: Hash Divergence\n```\nDifferent compressed bytes → different block boundaries → different hashes\n```\n- Even 1 byte difference in compression → all subsequent blocks shift\n- Block hashes change completely\n- Manifest becomes invalid for the new compression\n\n### Step 7: Silent Corruption\n```\nReceiver's bitmap (old hashes) + Sender's new hashes = mismatch\n```\n- Receiver's persisted bitmap references old block hashes\n- Sender emits frames with new block hashes\n- **Result:** Transfer completes but fails hash verification OR silently corrupts\n\n## Architectural Impact\n\n### Statelessness Violation\n\n**WITHOUT compression (stateless):**\n```\nFile → Blocks → Hashes\nSame file + same params = same hashes (deterministic)\nSender can restart and resume safely\n```\n\n**WITH compression (NOT stateless):**\n```\nFile → CompressionStream → Staging → Blocks → Hashes\nCompression is non-deterministic → different staging bytes → different hashes\nSender requires persistent staging to maintain hash consistency\nBut T4a requires staging to be wiped → contradiction\n```\n\n### Code Paths Affected\n\n1. **Sender block partitioning** (`src/core/block/partition.ts`)\n   - Must read from compressed staging, not original file\n   - Block boundaries depend on compressed bytes\n\n2. **Manifest generation** (Beacon frame, §7.6)\n   - Block hashes derived from compressed staging\n   - Different staging → different manifest\n\n3. **Receiver bitmap persistence** (D22, §8.3)\n   - Persists completed block indices\n   - Assumes hashes remain stable across restart\n\n4. **Resume logic** (Session state machine)\n   - `isResumeDisabled()` checks `Compressed` flag\n   - Suppresses resume UI when compression enabled\n\n## CompressionStream Determinism Analysis\n\n### Test Findings\n\nTests in `test/compression-determinism.test.ts` demonstrate:\n\n1. **CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee**\n   - The Web Compression API spec provides no stability promises\n   - Different browser versions may implement different algorithms\n   - Cross-platform consistency is not guaranteed\n\n2. **Gzip format considerations**\n   - RFC 1952: \"The format has no provision for interoperable compressed data\"\n   - Gzip can include optional metadata (filename, timestamp, comment)\n   - Compression level and strategy can affect output\n\n3. **Observed behavior**\n   - In our test environment (Node.js), compression appeared deterministic\n   - This is NOT guaranteed in browsers across versions/platforms\n   - Relying on observed determinism is a security/stability risk\n\n### Spec References\n\nFrom [CompressionStream](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CompressionStream):\n> \"The CompressionStream interface of the Compression Streams API compresses a stream of data.\"\n\n**No mention of:**\n- Determinism guarantees\n- Cross-version stability\n- Platform consistency\n- Reproducibility requirements\n\n## Implementation Status\n\n### Beacon Flags (src/core/frame/beacon.ts)\n\n```typescript\nexport enum BeaconFlags {\n  None = 0,\n  /** Compression enabled (D8) */\n  Compressed = 1 << 0,\n  /** Resume disabled when compression is enabled */\n  ResumeDisabled = 1 << 1,\n  // ...\n}\n```\n\n### Resume Logic (beacon.ts:311)\n\n```typescript\nexport function isResumeDisabled(flags: number): boolean {\n  return (flags & BeaconFlags.Compressed) !== 0;\n}\n```\n\n### Session Types (src/core/session/types.ts)\n\nReceiver states include:\n- `ReceivingState` - Normal operation\n- `PausedState` - Can resume if compression disabled\n- `CompleteState` - Final state, may have used compression\n\n### Plan.md Status (§8.3)\n\nThe plan already documents this:\n> \"The sender is stateless across restarts by construction (D24) **when compression is disabled** — it needs only the same file and the same `streamId` (§7.4). **With compression enabled, resume is NOT supported** — see `notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md`\"\n\n## User Experience Impact\n\n### Compression ON (Resume Disabled)\n- **Pros:** Faster transfers (3-10× less data to transmit)\n- **Cons:** No resume — interruptions restart from beginning\n- **Use case:** Stable connections, shorter transfers (< 1 hour)\n\n### Compression OFF (Resume Enabled)\n- **Pros:** Robust to interruptions — resume from last completed block\n- **Cons:** Slower transfers (full file size transmitted)\n- **Use case:** Multi-hour transfers, unstable connections\n\n## Testing Requirements\n\n### Implemented Tests\n\n✅ `test/compression-determinism.test.ts`\n- Documents CompressionStream behavior\n- Shows architectural problem with hash divergence\n- Tests statelessness violation\n\n### Integration Tests Needed\n\n1. **Compressed transfer interrupted → resume refused**\n   ```typescript\n   // Send with compression, stop at 50%, restart\n   // Assert: Resume UI shows \"Resume unavailable with compression\"\n   ```\n\n2. **Uncompressed transfer interrupted → resume succeeds**\n   ```typescript\n   // Send without compression, stop at 50%, restart\n   // Assert: Resume UI appears and completes successfully\n   ```\n\n3. **Beacon flag validation**\n   ```typescript\n   // Assert: Compressed beacon sets RESUME_DISABLED flag\n   // Assert: Receiver suppresses resume UI when flag set\n   ```\n\n## Alternative Approaches Considered\n\n### 1. Preserve Compressed Staging Across Restarts\n\n**Rejected because:**\n- Violates T4a privacy requirement (staging must be wiped)\n- Complicates sender statelessness\n- Orphaned staging accumulation on crashes\n- Cross-platform instability remains\n\n### 2. Deterministic Compression Implementation\n\n**Rejected because:**\n- Would require custom gzip implementation (maintenance burden)\n- Still vulnerable to browser runtime changes\n- Defeats the purpose of using native CompressionStream API\n- Adds complexity without guaranteed benefit\n\n### 3. Hash-Based Compression Verification\n\n**Rejected because:**\n- Requires storing compressed staging to verify hash\n- Brings us back to preserving staging (violates T4a)\n- Adds complexity without solving the root issue\n\n## Security and Privacy Considerations\n\n### T4a Compliance (Sender-side Staging)\n\nCurrent implementation is compliant:\n- Staging is reaped on startup (E11)\n- Staging is wiped on completion/cancel (T4a)\n- Resume disabled with compression → no persistent state needed\n\n### T4b Compliance (Receiver-side Output)\n\nPer `bf-1yk1`:\n- Receiver output follows deletion lifecycle\n- Orphan reaping on startup\n- User-visible delete controls\n- Warnings for partial artefacts\n\n## Documentation Updates Completed\n\n✅ **Plan.md §8.3** - Already documents the restriction\n✅ **Beacon flags** - `RESUME_DISABLED` implemented\n✅ **Session types** - Compression state tracked\n✅ **Test coverage** - Determinism tests added\n\n## References\n\n- **Plan §8.3** - Resume specification\n- **Plan §12 T4a** - Sender-side staging privacy\n- **Plan §12 T4b** - Receiver-side output lifecycle\n- **Plan D8** - Compression to staging file\n- **Plan E11** - Abandoned staging reaping\n- **Beacon format (§7.2)** - Flags specification\n- **`bf-17s0`** - Resume/Compression/T4-reap conflict resolution\n- **`bf-1yk1`** - T4b deletion lifecycle\n\n## Conclusion\n\nThe interaction between compression, resume, and T4 privacy requirements creates an architectural contradiction:\n\n1. **Resume requires statelessness** → Same inputs must produce same outputs\n2. **Compression is non-deterministic** → Same inputs may produce different outputs\n3. **T4 requires staging cleanup** → Cannot preserve compression state\n\n**Solution:** Explicitly disable resume when compression is enabled. Users choose between:\n- **Compression:** Speed, no resume\n- **No compression:** Robustness, with resume\n\nThis is documented in plan.md §8.3, implemented in beacon flags, and tested in `compression-determinism.test.ts`.\n","numLines":286,"startLine":1,"totalLines":286}}}

Startup Reaping of Orphaned Outputs\nOn application startup:\n- Scan OPFS for output artefacts that were not cleaned up (crashes, tab kills, navigation away)\n- Reap orphans older than a threshold (e.g., 24 hours) or offer user choice\n- Provide a UI indicator when orphaned files exist\n- Allow user to recover or delete orphaned files\n\n### 3. Warning Before Keeping Partial Artefacts\nWhen keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15):\n- **E10 (OPFS quota exhausted):** Export partial file + missing manifest\n  - Show explicit warning: \"This is an incomplete file. It will be stored until you delete it.\"\n  - Require user acknowledgment before keeping the partial artefact\n  - Mark the artefact clearly as \"partial\" in the UI\n- **E15 (Decompression failure):** Keep compressed artefact\n  - Show explicit warning: \"Decompression failed. The raw data will be stored until you delete it.\"\n  - Require user acknowledgment before keeping the artefact\n  - Mark the artefact clearly as \"compressed/raw\" in the UI\n\n### 4. User-Visible Delete Control\nProvide in-band deletion controls:\n- **Files list screen:** Show all stored output files (complete, partial, compressed)\n- **Per-file actions:** Delete button for each artefact\n- **Bulk actions:** \"Delete all\" option\n- **Clear indication:** Show file size, type, and age to help users decide\n- **Confirmation:** Require confirmation for deletion (non-recoverable)\n\n## Implementation Requirements\n\n### Storage Layer (`src/platform/storage.ts`)\n\n```typescript\ninterface OutputArtefact {\n  id: string;              // Unique identifier (e.g., streamId-based)\n  filename: string;        // Sanitised original filename\n  mimeType: string;        // Declared MIME type\n  size: number;           // Actual size in OPFS\n  status: 'complete' | 'partial' | 'compressed';\n  createdAt: number;      // Timestamp when created\n  streamId?: number;      // Associated stream ID for debugging\n  missingBlocks?: number[]; // For partial artefacts (E10)\n}\n\ninterface StorageManager {\n  // Write completed file to OPFS\n  writeOutput(streamId: number, filename: string, data: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;\n  \n  // Delete after successful export\n  deleteOutput(streamId: number): Promise<void>;\n  \n  // Startup reap of orphans\n  reapOrphans(maxAge?: number): Promise<OutputArtefact[]>;\n  \n  // List all artefacts for UI\n  listOutputs(): Promise<OutputArtefact[]>;\n  \n  // Keep partial artefact with warning\n  keepPartial(streamId: number, partialData: Uint8Array, missing: number[]): Promise<void>;\n}\n```\n\n### Key Implementation Points\n\n1. **Naming convention:** OPFS filenames should be obfuscated (not the original filename) to avoid leaking file metadata. Use a streamId-based naming scheme.\n\n2. **Metadata persistence:** Maintain a small manifest mapping streamId → artefact metadata. This manifest lives in OPFS alongside the files.\n\n3. **Delete timing:** \n   - Delete immediately after successful `share()` or `save()` resolves\n   - Do NOT wait for tab close (unreliable)\n   - Do NOT wait for manual cleanup (security exposure)\n\n4. **Reap strategy:**\n   - On startup, read the manifest\n   - For each artefact, check `createdAt` against current time\n   - Auto-reap artefacts older than threshold (default: 24 hours)\n   - Show UI notification for artefacts below threshold\n\n5. **Partial artefact handling:**\n   - Store with the `OutputArtefact.status = 'partial'` flag\n   - Include `missingBlocks` array for potential future resume\n   - UI should show clearly: \"Incomplete file (X of Y blocks received)\"\n\n## Integration with Edge Cases\n\n### E10: OPFS Quota Exhausted\n```typescript\n// When quota exhaustion occurs\nasync function handleQuotaExhausted(completedBlocks: Map<number, Uint8Array>, missing: number[]) {\n  // Export partial file + manifest of missing blocks\n  const partialData = concatenateBlocks(completedBlocks);\n  \n  // Show warning to user\n  const acknowledged = await showWarning(\n    \"Out of space. Partial file will be stored until you delete it.\"\n  );\n  \n  if (acknowledged) {\n    await storage.keepPartial(streamId, partialData, missing);\n    // Offer export of partial file + missing manifest\n    exportPartialFile(partialData, missing);\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### E15: Decompression Failure\n```typescript\n// When decompression fails at the end\nasync function handleDecompressionFailure(compressedData: Uint8Array) {\n  // Show warning to user\n  const acknowledged = await showWarning(\n    \"Decompression failed. Raw data will be stored until you delete it.\"\n  );\n  \n  if (acknowledged) {\n    await storage.keepCompressed(streamId, compressedData);\n    // Offer export of compressed artefact\n    exportCompressedFile(compressedData);\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Testing Requirements\n\n### Integration Tests\n\n1. **Successful completion:**\n   ```typescript\n   // Assert: receiver OPFS empty after These orphaned files accumulate over time, consuming storage quota with no way to recover them.\n\n## Solution\n\nOn app startup, scan for and automatically delete orphaned output files.\n\n## Orphan Criteria\n\nAn output file is considered orphaned when **BOTH** conditions are met:\n\n1. **No active session reference**: The file's `streamId` is not in the set of currently active session IDs\n2. **Older than max age**: The file's `createdAt` timestamp exceeds `maxOrphanAge` (default: 24 hours)\n\nThe age threshold prevents false positives during:\n- Normal app restart (e.g., browser update, device reboot)\n- Session resume (D22) where a paused session becomes active again\n- Brief app closure during long transfers\n\n## Implementation\n\n### Storage Manager (`src/platform/storage.ts`)\n\n**`OPFSStorageManager.cleanupOrphanedOutputs(activeStreamIds: Set<number>)`**\n\n- Lists all output metadata files (`.meta.json`)\n- Checks each output against orphan criteria\n- Deletes both data file (`.bin`) and metadata file (`.meta.json`)\n- Returns count of files cleaned up\n- Logs each deletion with file details (streamId, filename, age)\n\n**`runStartupCleanup(activeStreamIds: Set<number>)`**\n\n- Convenience wrapper around storage manager\n- Returns `{ cleaned: number, error?: string }`\n- Handles errors gracefully (returns 0 cleaned on failure)\n\n### App Initialization (`src/platform/init.ts`)\n\n**`runAppInit()`**\n\n- Runs startup cleanup in parallel with health check\n- Uses empty `Set()` for active stream IDs (no active sessions on startup)\n- Returns `InitResult` with `orphanedOutputsCleaned` count\n- Logs initialization results (health status, cleanup count, errors)\n\n**Non-blocking execution**: Cleanup runs in Promise.all with health check, so UI loads immediately without waiting for cleanup to complete.\n\n## Configuration\n\n### StorageManagerConfig\n\n```typescript\n{\n  outputDirectory: string;      // OPFS subdirectory (default: 'screenferry-outputs')\n  maxOrphanAge: number;        // Max age for orphans in ms (default: 24 hours)\n}\n```\n\n### Custom Configuration\n\n```typescript\nimport { configureStorageManager } from './platform/storage.js';\n\n// Must be called before first getStorageManager() call\nconfigureStorageManager({\n  outputDirectory: 'custom-outputs',\n  maxOrphanAge: 60 * 60 * 1000, // 1 hour\n});\n```\n\n## Usage\n\n### During App Initialization\n\n```typescript\nimport { runAppInit } from './platform/init.js';\n\n// Called during app startup\nconst result = await runAppInit();\n\nconsole.log(`Cleaned ${result.orphanedOutputsCleaned} orphaned files`);\n```\n\n### Manual Cleanup (Advanced)\n\n```typescript\nimport { getStorageManager } from './platform/storage.js';\n\nconst storage = getStorageManager();\nconst activeIds = new Set<number>([123, 456]); // Currently active streams\nconst cleaned = await storage.cleanupOrphanedOutputs(activeIds);\n```\n\n## Testing\n\n### Unit Tests (`test/storage.test.ts`)\n\n- **Age-based orphan detection**: Removes files older than max age\n- **Active session protection**: Keeps files in active set regardless of age\n- **Recent file protection**: Keeps recent files even if not active\n- **Empty storage handling**: Handles no-op case gracefully\n- **Mixed age handling**: Correctly filters mixed-age files\n- **Error handling**: Continues cleanup even if individual deletions fail\n- **Configuration options**: Respects custom `maxOrphanAge`\n\n### Integration Tests (`test/init.test.ts`)\n\n- **Parallel execution**: Runs cleanup alongside health check\n- **Error collection**: Collects errors from both cleanup and health check\n- **Result formatting**: Formats user-friendly status messages\n- **Logging verification**: Verifies console output\n\n## Metrics and Logging\n\n### Console Logs\n\n```\n[Storage] Starting orphaned output cleanup...\n[Storage] Cleaning up orphaned output: streamId=123, filename=test.dat, age=45 minutes\n[Storage] Deleted output: streamId=123\n[Storage] Cleanup complete: removed 3 orphaned output(s)\n[Init] Initialization complete in 234ms\n[Init] Health check: PASSED\n[Init] Orphaned outputs cleaned: 3\n```\n\n### Return Values\n\n- `runAppInit()` → `InitResult` with `orphanedOutputsCleaned` count\n- `cleanupOrphanedOutputs()` → `number` (count of files removed)\n- `runStartupCleanup()` → `{ cleaned: number, error?: string }`\n\n## Security Considerations\n\n- **Same-origin restriction**: OPFS is origin-private, no cross-origin access\n- **No user data exposure**: Cleanup only removes app's own output files\n- **No active session disruption**: Age threshold prevents deleting recent files that might be in use\n\n## Performance\n\n- **Non-blocking**: Runs in background, doesn't block app initialization\n- **Incremental**: Processes files one at a time, no large memory allocations\n- **Fast for typical usage**: Most apps have 0-2 orphaned files\n- **Graceful degradation**: Continues on individual deletion failures\n\n## Future Enhancements\n\n- **Configurable age threshold**: Allow users to set custom orphan age in settings\n- **Manual cleanup button**: UI button to trigger cleanup on demand\n- **Cleanup statistics**: Track cleanup frequency and file age distribution\n- **User notification**: Show toast when orphans are cleaned up\n\n## References\n\n- **Storage implementation**: `src/platform/storage.ts`\n- **Init integration**: `src/platform/init.ts`\n- **Session types**: `src/core/session/types.ts`\n- **Tests**: `test/storage.test.ts`, `test/init.test.ts`\n- **Bead**: bf-ho40\n\n## Why: \n\nWithout automatic cleanup, orphaned files accumulate indefinitely:\n- Each incomplete transfer leaves a partial file in OPFS\n- OPFS quota is limited (typically ~50-60% of total storage)\n- No built-in cleanup mechanism in browsers\n- Manual cleanup requires developer tools or browser data clearing\n\n## How to apply:\n\nThe cleanup is automatic and runs on every app startup.
